decomposeMatrix.haxe_doc: Extract the rotation from `inMatrix` and stores it as a quaternion inside the [m12,m13,m21,m23] component instead of the rotation being mixed with the scale.

recomposeMatrix.haxe_doc: Inverts the operation of `decomposeMatrix`, giving back a normal transformation matrix from a decomposed one

lookAtXInline.haxe_doc: Build a rotation Matrix so the X axis will look at the given direction, and the Z axis will be the Up vector ([0,0,1] by default)
Build a rotation Matrix so the X axis will look at the given direction, and the Z axis will be the Up vector ([0,0,1] by default)

pow.haxe_doc: Makes a unit quaternion to the power of the value.

negate.haxe_doc: Negate the quaternion: this will not change the actual angle, use `conjugate` for that.

weightedBlend.haxe_doc: Blends the sourceQuats together with the given weights and store the result in `this`. ReferenceQuat is the default rotation to use as the base for the blend (for example the default rotation of a bone in a skeletal mesh)

class.haxe_doc: A 3 floats vector. Everytime a Vector is returned, it means a copy is created.

abstract.haxe_doc: A 3 floats vector. Everytime a Vector is returned, it means a copy is created.

class.haxe_doc: A 4 floats vector. Everytime a Vector is returned, it means a copy is created.

abstract.haxe_doc: A 4 floats vector. Everytime a Vector is returned, it means a copy is created. For function manipulating the length (length, normalize, dot, scale, etc.), the Vector acts like a Point in the sense only the X/Y/Z components will be affected.

bind.haxe_doc: If one of the animated object has been changed, it is necessary to call bind() so the animation can keep with the change.

getPropValue.haxe_doc: Returns the current value of animation property for the given object, or null if not found.

sync.haxe_doc: Synchronize the target object matrix. If decompose is true, then the rotation quaternion is stored in [m12,m13,m21,m23] instead of mixed with the scale.

criticalSpringDamper.haxe_doc: x : the current value v : the current velocity of the value xGoal : the target value we want to reach vGoal : the target velocity we want to reach halfLife: the time in seconds that the x value will take to reach half the distance to xGoal dt : the delta time since the last call of this function

simpleSpringDamper.haxe_doc: Same as criticalSpringDamper but with vGoal = 0

x.haxe_doc: X Position of the blend point in the Blendspace

xSmooth.haxe_doc: Smooth factor for the X value position over time

y.haxe_doc: Y Position of the blend point in the BlendSpace

ySmooth.haxe_doc: Smooth factor for the Y value position over time

scaleSpeedOutsideOfBounds.haxe_doc: If true, the speed of the blended animation will be scaled when the x/y points lies outside all of the blend space triangles, based on the distance of the point from the center of the graph (0,0) and the distance of the closest point inside of the graph to the center

class.haxe_doc: Blends multiple animations points placed on a virtual 2d plane

retargetAnim.haxe_doc: When animated, we will use the default bind pose translation instead of the animated translation, enabling retargeting on a skeleton with different proportions

rayIntersection.haxe_doc: Returns the distance of intersection between the ray and the collider, or negative if no collision. If bestMatch is false, only negative/positive value needs to be returned, with no additional precision.

inFrustumDetails.haxe_doc: * Check if the camera model-view-projection Matrix intersects with the Bounds. Returns -1 if outside, 0 if intersects and 1 if fully inside. * @param mvp : the model-view-projection matrix to test against * @param checkZ : tells if we will check against the near/far plane

step.haxe_doc: When performing raycast check, tells by how much step we advance. If this is too small, raycast check will be too expensive. If this is too big, we might step through a hip without noticing. Default : 1.0

precision.haxe_doc: Tells which precision is required for the result. We will iterate until we have reach the given precision.

getZ.haxe_doc: Returns the height value at given coordinates.

class.haxe_doc: This is an helper class to define a heightmap-based collider. In order to use, you need to extends this class and override the getZ method in order to return appropriate Z value based on X and Y coordinates.
Wraps a collider so that a ray starting inside it hits it at distance 0, instead of missing it.

normalize.haxe_doc: Normalize the plan, so we can use distance().

distance.haxe_doc: Returns the signed distance between a point an the plane. This requires the plan to be normalized. If the distance is negative it means that we are "under" the plan.

currentAnimation.haxe_doc: The animation currently played on this object, or `null`. Set by `playAnimation` and `switchToAnimation`, cleared by `stopAnimation`.

parent.haxe_doc: The parent object in the scene tree.

numChildren.haxe_doc: How many immediate children this object has.

visible.haxe_doc: Is the object and its children are displayed on screen (default true).

culled.haxe_doc: Inform that the object is not to be displayed and his animation doesn't have to be sync. Unlike visible, this doesn't apply to children unless inheritCulled is set to true.

alwaysSyncAnimation.haxe_doc: When an object is not visible or culled, its animation does not get synchronized unless you set alwaysSyncAnimation=true

inheritCulled.haxe_doc: When enabled, the culled flag and culling collider is inherited by children objects.

ignoreBounds.haxe_doc: When enabled, the object bounds are ignored when using getBounds()

forceBounds.haxe_doc: When enabled, the object bounds are included even if it's not visible when using getBounds()

ignoreCollide.haxe_doc: When enabled, the object is ignored when using getCollider()

modelRoot.haxe_doc: Tag the object as a model root

ignoreParentTransform.haxe_doc: When enabled, the object will not follow its parent transform

lightCameraCenter.haxe_doc: When selecting the lights to apply to this object, we will use the camera target as reference instead of the object absolute position. This is useful for very large objects so they can get good lighting. (this is only relevant in forward rendering)

fixedPosition.haxe_doc: When set, the object and all its children will not sync() unless this root object position has been changed. This allows to optimize cpu cost of static objects having many children. When set, changes on position during sync() won't be applied.

alwaysSync.haxe_doc: When unset, the object and all its children will not sync() if this root object or one of its parent is culled or not visible. This allows to optimize cpu cost of objects having many children.

drawn.haxe_doc: When set, the object has been drawn during previous frame. Useful for temporal effects such as temporal antialiasing.

cullingCollider.haxe_doc: When set, collider shape will be used for automatic frustum culling. If `inheritCulled` is true, collider will be inherited to children unless they have their own collider set.

cullingColliderInherited.haxe_doc: Indicates that current cullingCollider is currently inherited from a parent object

x.haxe_doc: The x position of the object relative to its parent.

y.haxe_doc: The y position of the object relative to its parent.

z.haxe_doc: The z position of the object relative to its parent.

scaleX.haxe_doc: The amount of scaling along the X axis of this object (default 1.0)

scaleY.haxe_doc: The amount of scaling along the Y axis of this object (default 1.0)

scaleZ.haxe_doc: The amount of scaling along the Z axis of this object (default 1.0)

follow.haxe_doc: Follow a given object or joint as if it was our parent. Ignore defaultTransform when set.

followPositionOnly.haxe_doc: When follow is set, only follow the position and ignore both scale and rotation.

defaultTransform.haxe_doc: This is an additional optional transformation that is performed before other local transformations. It is used by the animation system.

name.haxe_doc: The name of the object, can be used to retrieve an object within a tree by using `getObjectByName` (default null)

playAnimation.haxe_doc: Create an animation instance bound to the object, set it as currentAnimation and play it.

switchToAnimation.haxe_doc: Change the current animation. This animation should be an instance that was previously created by playAnimation.

stopAnimation.haxe_doc: Stop the current animation. If recursive is set to true, all children will also stop their animation

applyAnimationTransform.haxe_doc: When an object is loaded, its position scale and rotation will always be set to the default values (0 for position/rotation and 1 for scale). If it's part of a group/scene or if it's animated, then its position/rotation/scale will be stored into the defaultTransform matrix. Calling this function will reset the defaultTransform to null and instead initialize x/y/z/rotation/scale properties. This will not change the actual position of the object but allows you to move the object more freely on your own. Do not use on an object that is currently being animated, since it will set again defaultTransform and apply twice the transformation.

getObjectsCount.haxe_doc: Return the total number of children, recursively.

getMaterialByName.haxe_doc: Search for a material recursively by name, return it or null if not found.

contains.haxe_doc: Tells if the object is contained into this object children, recursively.

find.haxe_doc: Find a single object in the tree by calling `f` on each and returning the first not-null value returned, or null if not found.

findAll.haxe_doc: Find several objects in the tree by calling `f` on each and returning all the not-null values returned.

getMaterials.haxe_doc: Return all materials in the tree.

localToGlobal.haxe_doc: Convert a local position (or [0,0] if pt is null) relative to the object origin into an absolute global position, applying all the inherited transforms.

globalToLocal.haxe_doc: Convert an absolute global position into a local position relative to the object origin, applying all the inherited transforms.

getInvPos.haxe_doc: Returns the updated inverse position matrix. Please note that this is not a copy and should not be modified.

getBounds.haxe_doc: Return the bounds of this object and all its children, in absolute global coordinates or relative to the object being used as parameter.

getMeshes.haxe_doc: Return all meshes part of this tree

getMeshByName.haxe_doc: Search for an mesh recursively by name, return null if not found.

getObjectByName.haxe_doc: Search for an object recursively by name, return null if not found.

clone.haxe_doc: Make a copy of the object and all its children.

addChild.haxe_doc: Add a child object at the end of the children list.

addChildAt.haxe_doc: Insert a child object at the specified position of the children list.

iterVisibleMeshes.haxe_doc: Iterate on all mesh that are currently visible and not culled in the tree. Call `callb` for each mesh found.

removeChild.haxe_doc: Remove the given object from our immediate children list if it's part of it.

removeChildren.haxe_doc: Remove all children from our immediate children list

remove.haxe_doc: Same as parent.removeChild(this), but does nothing if parent is null. In order to capture add/removal from scene, you can override onAdd/onRemove/onParentChanged

getScene.haxe_doc: Return the Scene this object is part of, or null if not added to a Scene.

getAbsPos.haxe_doc: Returns the updated absolute position matrix. Please note that this is not a copy so it should not be modified.

getRelPos.haxe_doc: Returns the position matrix relative to another scene object

isMesh.haxe_doc: Tell if the object is a Mesh.

toMesh.haxe_doc: If the object is a Mesh, return the corresponding Mesh. If not, throw an exception.

getCollider.haxe_doc: Build and return the global absolute recursive collider for the object. Returns null if no collider was found or if ignoreCollide was set to true.

getGlobalCollider.haxe_doc: Same as getLocalCollider, but returns an absolute collider instead of a local one.

getLocalCollider.haxe_doc: Build and returns the local relative not-recursive collider for the object, or null if this object does not have a collider. Does not check for ignoreCollide.

getPosition.haxe_doc: Return the (x,y,z) position relative to the object parent.

setPosition.haxe_doc: Set the position of the object relative to its parent.

setTransform.haxe_doc: Set the position, scale and rotation of the object relative to its parent based on the specified transform matrix.

getTransform.haxe_doc: Returns the local position, scale and rotation of the object relative to its parent.

rotate.haxe_doc: Rotate around the current rotation axis by the specified angles (in radian).

setRotation.haxe_doc: Set the rotation using the specified angles (in radian).

setRotationAxis.haxe_doc: Set the rotation using the specified axis and angle of rotation around it (in radian).

setDirection.haxe_doc: Set the rotation using the specified look at direction

getLocalDirection.haxe_doc: Return the direction in which the object rotation is currently oriented to

getRotationQuat.haxe_doc: Return the quaternion representing the current object rotation. Dot not modify as it's not a copy.

setRotationQuat.haxe_doc: Set the quaternion representing the current object rotation. Dot not modify the value afterwards as no copy is made.

scale.haxe_doc: Scale uniformly the object by the given factor.

setScale.haxe_doc: Set the uniform scale for the object.

toString.haxe_doc: Return both class name and object name if any.

getChildAt.haxe_doc: Return the `n`th element among our immediate children list, or null if there is no.

getChildIndex.haxe_doc: Return the index of the object `o` within our immediate children list, or `-1` if it is not part of our children list.

iterator.haxe_doc: Return an iterator over this object immediate children

new.haxe_doc: Create a new empty object, and adds it to the parent object if not null.

class.haxe_doc: h3d.scene.Object is the base 3D class that all scene tree elements inherit from. It can be used to create a virtual container that does not display anything but can contain other objects so the various transforms are inherited to its children.

TimeStamp.haxe_doc: The result will give the GPU Timestamp (in nanoseconds, 1e-9 seconds) at the time the endQuery is performed

Samples.haxe_doc: The result will give the number of samples that passes the depth buffer between beginQuery/endQuery range

TimeElapsed.haxe_doc: The result will give the GPU elapsed time (in nanoseconds, 1e-9 seconds) between beginQuery/endQuery range

CameraHandness.haxe_doc: 0 = LeftHanded (default), 1 = RightHanded. Affects the meaning of triangle culling value.

copyTexture.haxe_doc: Returns true if we could copy the texture, false otherwise (not supported by driver or mismatch in size/format)

setResidentMip.haxe_doc: Reallocates the allocated texture so its most detailed mip level is `mip`, keeping the content of the mip levels common to both allocations. Returns false if not supported or out of memory, in which case the texture is unchanged. Requires the ResidentMips feature.

maxFps.haxe_doc: maxFps will be set automatically to *2 or /2. Default value is chosen for 30FPS(45), 60FPS(90), 144FPS(180)

begin.haxe_doc: Call at the begining of a hxd.App's `update` for CPU/GPU time

end.haxe_doc: Call at the end of a hxd.App's `render` for CPU/GPU time

outOfMemoryCheck.haxe_doc: Perform OUT_OF_MEMORY checks when allocating textures/buffers. Default true, except in WebGL (false)

ELEMENT_SIZE.haxe_doc: Bytes are structures of 5 i32 with the following values: - indexCount : number of indexes per instance - instanceCount : number of indexed draws - startIndexLocation : offset in indexes - baseVertexLocation : offset in buffer - startInstanceLocation : offset in per instance buffer

autoDisposeKeepTime.haxe_doc: How much time a texture should be kept into memory if it's not used.

autoDisposeGpuFreeMB.haxe_doc: The amount of free memory we want to keep on our GPU to allow swapping.

garbage.haxe_doc: Call user-defined garbage function that will cleanup some unused allocated objects. Might be called several times if we need to allocate a lot of memory

allocStats.haxe_doc: * Return statistics for currently allocated buffers and textures. * Requires call `MemoryManager.enableTrackAlloc()` before allocations.

Target.haxe_doc: Allocate a texture that will be used as render target.

Cube.haxe_doc: Allocate a cube texture. Might be restricted to power of two textures only.

MipMapped.haxe_doc: Activates Mip Mapping for this texture. Might not be available for target textures.

ManualMipMapGen.haxe_doc: By default, textures created with MipMapped will have their mipmaps generated when you upload the mipmap level 0. This flag disables this and manually upload mipmaps instead.

IsNPOT.haxe_doc: This is a not power of two texture. Automatically set when having width or height being not power of two.

NoAlloc.haxe_doc: Don't initialy allocate the texture memory.

Dynamic.haxe_doc: Inform that we will often perform upload operations on this texture

AlphaPremultiplied.haxe_doc: Assumes that the color value of the texture is premultiplied by the alpha component.

WasCleared.haxe_doc: Tells if the target texture has been cleared (reserved for internal engine usage).

Loading.haxe_doc: The texture is being currently loaded. Set onLoaded to get event when loading is complete.

Serialize.haxe_doc: Allow texture data serialization when found in a scene (for user generated textures)

IsArray.haxe_doc: Tells if it's a texture array

AsyncLoading.haxe_doc: Allows a DDS texture to be loaded asynchronously (see hxd.res.Image.ASYNC_LOADING)

LazyLoading.haxe_doc: By default, the texture are loaded from images when created. If this flag is enabled, the texture will be loaded from disk when first used.

Writable.haxe_doc: Texture can be written in shaders using RWTexture

dynamicParameters.haxe_doc: Inform the pass system that the parameters will be modified in object draw() command, so they will be manually uploaded by calling RenderContext.uploadParams.

isStatic.haxe_doc: Mark the pass as static, this will allow some renderers or shadows to filter it when rendering static/dynamic parts.

addShaderAtIndex.haxe_doc: Can be used for internal usage

getDefaultDepth.haxe_doc: This will return the default depth buffer, which is automatically resized to the screen size.

fromColor.haxe_doc: Creates a 1x1 texture using the RGB color passed as parameter.

defaultCubeTexture.haxe_doc: Returns a default dummy 1x1 black cube texture

genChecker.haxe_doc: Returns a checker texture of size x size, than can be repeated

residentMip.haxe_doc: The most detailed mip level allocated on the GPU : mip levels before it are not allocated, and the texture is sampled starting at this level.

isPlaceholder.haxe_doc: A 1x1 texture is allocated while the texture is loading (see hxd.res.Image)

realloc.haxe_doc: If this callback is set, the texture can be re-allocated when the 3D context has been lost or when it's been free because of lack of memory.

depthBuffer.haxe_doc: When the texture is used as render target, tells which depth buffer will be used. If set to null, depth testing is disabled.

preventAutoDispose.haxe_doc: In case we run out of GPU memory, textures that hasn't been used for a long time will be disposed. Calling this will make this texture not considered for auto disposal.

waitLoad.haxe_doc: Some textures might take some time to load. You can check flags.has(Loading) or add a waitLoad callback which will get called either immediately if the texture is already loaded or when loading is complete.

capturePixels.haxe_doc: Downloads the current texture data from the GPU. Beware, this is a very slow operation that shouldn't be done during rendering.

currentInstance.haxe_doc: Set when initializing hxd.Res, or manually. Allows code to resolve resources without compiling hxd.Res

DEFAULT_RESOLVER.haxe_doc:
This value can be set to use custom type resolvers.
A type resolver finds a `Class` or `Enum` instance from a given `String`. By default, the Haxe `Type` Api is used.
A type resolver must provide two methods:
1. `resolveClass(name:String):Class<Dynamic>` is called to determine a `Class` from a class name 2. `resolveEnum(name:String):Enum<Dynamic>` is called to determine an `Enum` from an enum name
This value is applied when a new `Unserializer` instance is created. Changing it afterwards has no effect on previously created instances.

run.haxe_doc:
Unserializes `v` and returns the according value.
This is a convenience function for creating a new instance of Unserializer with `v` as buffer and calling its `unserialize()` method once.

unserialize.haxe_doc:
Unserializes the next part of `this` Unserializer instance and returns the according value.
This function may call `this.resolver.resolveClass` to determine a Class from a String, and `this.resolver.resolveEnum` to determine an Enum from a String.
If `this` Unserializer instance contains no more or invalid data, an exception is thrown.
This operation may fail on structurally valid data if a type cannot be resolved or if a field cannot be set. This can happen when unserializing Strings that were serialized on a different Haxe target, in which the serialization side has to make sure not to include platform-specific data.
Classes are created from `Type.createEmptyInstance`, which means their constructors are not called.

new.haxe_doc:
Creates a new Unserializer instance, with its internal buffer initialized to `buf`.
This does not parse `buf` immediately. It is parsed only when calls to `this.unserialize` are made.
Each Unserializer instance maintains its own cache.

class.haxe_doc:
The `Unserializer` class is the complement to the `Serializer` class. It parses a serialization `String` and creates objects from the contained data.
This class can be used in two ways:
- create a `new Unserializer()` instance with a given serialization String, then call its `unserialize()` method until all values are extracted - call `Unserializer.run()` to unserialize a single value from a given String
The specification of the serialization format can be found here: <https://haxe.org/manual/serialization/format>

primitive.haxe_doc: The primitive of the mesh: the list of vertexes and indices necessary to display the mesh.

material.haxe_doc: The material of the mesh: the properties used to display it (texture, color, shaders, etc.)

inheritLod.haxe_doc: When enabled, the lod level is inherited by children objects.

blendshapeInstance.haxe_doc: Instance of the blendshape of the mesh: the list of weights for the different shapes

forcedLod.haxe_doc: Allow user to force a specific lod index. If set to -1, forced lod will be ignored.

getMeshMaterials.haxe_doc: Return all materials for the current object.

getLodIndex.haxe_doc: Returns the level of detail currently used to draw this mesh: `forcedLod` if set (not `-1`), otherwise the LOD selected by the primitive from the screen ratio computed during the last frame.

setBlendshapeWeight.haxe_doc: Sets the weight of the blend shape (morph target) `name`. The primitive must be a `h3d.prim.HMDModel` with blend shapes.

setBlendshapeWeights.haxe_doc: Sets the weights of all the blend shapes at once, in the order returned by `getBlenshapeNames`.

getBlenshapeNames.haxe_doc: Returns the names of the blend shapes of the primitive, or an empty array if it has none.

hasBlendshapes.haxe_doc: Tells if the primitive of this mesh has blend shapes (morph targets).

new.haxe_doc: Creates a new mesh with given primitive, material and parent object. If material is not specified, a new default material is created for the current renderer.

class.haxe_doc: h3d.scene.Mesh is the base class for all 3D objects displayed on screen. Unlike Object base class, all properties of Mesh only apply to the current object and are not inherited by its children.

offsetParticles.haxe_doc: Offset all existing particles by the given values.

Dynamic.haxe_doc: Particles are sorted back-to-front every frame based on their current position.

Point.haxe_doc: A single Point, emit in all directions

Cone.haxe_doc: A cone, parametrized with emitAngle and emitDistance

CameraBounds.haxe_doc: Same as VolumeBounds, but in Camera space, not world space.

Disc.haxe_doc: A disc, emit in one direction

materials.haxe_doc: The materials, indexed by primitive material group. `null` entries are not drawn. `Mesh.material` refers to the first one.

class.haxe_doc:
A `Mesh` using several materials, one per material group of its primitive.
The primitive must split its indexes per material (for instance a `h3d.prim.HMDModel` loaded from a model with several materials): each material `i` is drawn with the indexes of group `i`.

PFORMAT.expr: hxd.BufferFormat.make([{ name : "position", type : DVec3 }, { name : "normal", type : DVec3 }, { name : "uv", type : DVec2 }, { name : "time", type : DFloat }, { name : "life", type : DFloat }, { name : "init", type : DVec2 }, { name : "delta", type : DVec2 }])

amount.haxe_doc: Tells how much percent of the particles to display. This can be used to progressively display a particle effect. This can also be done per group in GpuPartGroup.progress

uploadedCount.haxe_doc: Tells how many particles were uploaded to GPU last frame (for performance tuning).

count.haxe_doc: Tells how many particles are live actually

radius.haxe_doc: How far in pixels the blur will go.

gain.haxe_doc: How much the blur increases or decreases the color amount (default = 1)

linear.haxe_doc: Set linear blur instead of gaussian (default = 0).

quality.haxe_doc: Adjust how much quality/speed tradeoff we want (default = 1)

needStaticUpdate.haxe_doc: * Triggers update of static part of shadows (if any).

maxDist.haxe_doc: Clamp the zFar of the frustum of the camera for bounds calculation

autoShrink.haxe_doc: Shrink the frustum of the light to the bounds containing all visible objects

autoZPlanes.haxe_doc: For top down lights and cameras, use scene Z min/max to optimize shadowmap. Requires autoShrink

maxDist.haxe_doc: Clamp the zFar of the frustum of the camera for bounds calculation

minDist.haxe_doc: Clamp the zNear of the frustum of the camera for bounds calculation

init.haxe_doc: Set the passes and empty the discarded list

reset.haxe_doc: Put back discarded passes into the pass list

save.haxe_doc: Save the discarded list, allow to perfom some filters, then call "load" to restore passes

load.haxe_doc: load state that was save() before

clear.haxe_doc: Put all passes into discarded list

filter.haxe_doc: Filter current passes, add results to discarded list

getFiltered.haxe_doc: Iterate on all discarded elements, if any

begin.haxe_doc: Call begin() before starting to add vertexes/indexes to the primitive. The count value is the number of vertexes you will add, it will automatically flush() if it doesn't fit into the current buffer.

addPoint.haxe_doc: This is similar to addVertexValue for X Y and Z, but will also update the bounds if you wish to have them calculated.

flush.haxe_doc: Flush the current buffer. It is required to call begin() after a flush()

m.e: { stride : -1, scale : 1., rotation : 0., dz : 0., dy : 0., dx : 0. }

add.haxe_doc: Adds a complete object to the primitive, with custom position,scale,rotation. See addSub for complete documentation.

m.e: { mat : null, color : 1., deltaV : 0., deltaU : 0., stride : -1, scale : 1., rotation : 0., dz : 0., dy : 0., dx : 0. }

addSub.haxe_doc: Adds a buffer to the primitive, with custom position,scale,rotation. The buffer can have more stride than the BigPrimitive, but not less. It is assumed that the buffer contains [X,Y,Z,NX,NY,NZ,U,V,R,G,B] (depending on his stride) so the different offsets are applied to the corresponding components. If hasTangent=true, we have [TX,TY,TZ] just after normal. However if the stride is 5, we assume [X,Y,Z,U,V] If mat is not null, it overrides dx, dy, dz, rotation, scale

class.haxe_doc: Vertex buffers are limited to 65K vertexes because of the 16-bits limitation of the index buffers. BigPrimitive allows you to easily create large buffers by spliting the buffers.

setUVCount.haxe_doc: Add additional Uv sets that are a copy of the base uv set

addUVs.haxe_doc: * Warning : This will splice four basic uv value but can provoke aliasing problems.

new.haxe_doc: * You have to pass vertices in this order: top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right

defaultUnitCylinder.haxe_doc: * Get a default unit Cylinder with * segs = 16, ray = 0.5, height = 1.0, centered = false * and add UVs to it. If it has not be cached, it is cached and subsequent * calls to this method will return Cylinder from cache. * @param segs Optional number of segments of the cylinder, default 16

defaultUnitDisc.haxe_doc: * Get a default unit Disc with * radius = 0.5, segments = 8, thetaStart = 0.0, thetaLength = Math.PI * 2 * and add UVs to it. If it has not be cached, it is cached and subsequent * calls to this method will return Disc from cache.

minVSize.haxe_doc: Minimum number of elements in vertex buffer

minISize.haxe_doc: Minimum number of elements in index index buffer

class.haxe_doc: Shader applying the animated transform of the source object to all the instances of an `AnimMeshBatch`.

shadersChanged.haxe_doc: Set if shader list or shader constants has changed, before calling begin()

instanceCount.haxe_doc: The number of instances on this batch

worldPosition.haxe_doc: * If set, use this position in emitInstance() instead MeshBatch absolute position

primitiveSubMeshes.haxe_doc: Tells the mesh batch to draw only a subpart of the primitive.

curSubMesh.haxe_doc: The index in `primitiveSubMeshes` of the sub mesh drawn by the next `emitInstance`.

cpuIndirectCallBuffers.haxe_doc: Use one indirect call buffer per material. Instances can not be culled for a specific pass yet.

calcBounds.haxe_doc: If set, exact bounds will be recalculated during emitInstance (default true)

curLod.haxe_doc: With EnableCpuLod, set the lod of the next emitInstance. Without EnableCpuLod and not using primitiveSubMeshes, set the lod of the whole batch.

enableStorageBuffer.haxe_doc: * Buffer of per instance params such as position is created as a storage buffer * allowing for huge amount of instances.

enableGpuUpdate.haxe_doc: * Buffer of per instance params such as position is created with its own format * allowing compute shaders to update those parameters.

forceGpuUpdate.haxe_doc: * Force PerInstance to be setup by a compute shader. * Don't support without Storage Buffer to simplify implementation.

enableSubMesh.haxe_doc: * Use sub mesh to emit instance. * Don't support multiple materials without Storage Buffer to simplify implementation.

enablePerInstanceTexture.haxe_doc: * Enable per instance texture if bindless is supported.

enableCpuLod.haxe_doc: Selects the level of detail of each instance on the CPU, according to its screen size (or `curLod` if set). Has no effect if the primitive has a single level of detail. Enables the storage buffer.

emitInstance.haxe_doc: Adds an instance using the current transform of the batch (or `worldPosition` if set) and the current values of the parameters of its shaders.

flush.haxe_doc: Uploads the emitted instances to the GPU. Called automatically during sync.

disposeBuffers.haxe_doc: Releases the GPU buffers of the instances. They are reallocated by the next `flush`.

class.haxe_doc: h3d.scene.MeshBatch allows to draw multiple meshed in a single draw call. See samples/MeshBatch.hx for an example.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a batch of `primitive` whose instances copy the animated local transform of `copyObject`.

class.haxe_doc: A `MeshBatch` whose instances all follow the animated transform of a source mesh (see `AnimMeshBatcher`).

Draws many copies of an animated object with instancing: one `MeshBatch` is created per mesh of the object, and all the copies play the same animation in sync.
Only the transform of each mesh is animated (rigid animations): skeletal deformation is not supported.

ManualEmitGPU.haxe_doc: The compute passes building the draw commands are not run automatically: call `Batcher.syncGPU` and `Batcher.emitGPU` yourself.

enum.haxe_doc: Options of a `Batcher`.

meshes.haxe_doc: The meshes of the model, with their transform relative to the model root.

draws.haxe_doc: The draw passes of the materials.

class.haxe_doc: A model registered in a `Batcher` with `Batcher.addInstance`, which can then be emitted many times.

addModel.haxe_doc: Adds the geometry of a model to the library.

addPolygon.haxe_doc: Adds the geometry of a polygon to the library.

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the GPU resources of the library.

checkOffsetBuffer.haxe_doc: Makes sure the per instance index buffer can hold `instanceCount` instances.

class.haxe_doc: The geometry storage shared by `Batcher` instances: the models are packed in one big primitive per vertex format. Share a library between several batchers drawing the same models to avoid duplicating the geometry.

emitInstance.haxe_doc: Adds an instance of `obj` to this group. See `Batcher.emitInstance`.

reserveInstances.haxe_doc: Preallocates `count` instances of `obj` in this group. See `Batcher.reserveInstances`.

remove.haxe_doc: Removes all the instances of this group and releases it.

class.haxe_doc: A group of instances of a `Batcher` which can be removed together. Created with `Batcher.createGroup`.

shadowMaxDistance.haxe_doc: If positive, instances farther than this distance are not drawn in the shadow passes.

shadowCameraFrustumCulling.haxe_doc: If `true`, the shadow passes only draw the instances inside the camera frustum (aggressive culling, faster but shadows of objects outside the view can disappear). Otherwise they draw the instances inside the area seen by the camera, extended towards the light by `shadowCullingOffset`.

shadowCullingOffset.haxe_doc: The distance the shadow casting area is extended towards the light, so that objects outside the view still cast shadows inside it.

hzbCulling.haxe_doc: Enables GPU occlusion culling using the hierarchical depth buffer built by the renderer (`RenderContext.hzb`).

isRelative.haxe_doc: If `true`, the instance positions are relative to the batcher transform, so the batcher can be moved. Otherwise they are in world space.

syncShader.haxe_doc: An optional compute shader updating the instance transforms on the GPU each frame (see `BaseSync`), run by `syncGPU`.

hasSyncIDs.haxe_doc: Tells if the `syncShader` uses per instance sync IDs.

addShader.haxe_doc: Adds a shader to all the instances. @param pass The name of the material pass to add the shader to, or `""` for the main pass of every material.

createGroup.haxe_doc: Creates a group of instances, which can be removed together with `BatchGroup.remove`.

reserveInstances.haxe_doc: Preallocates `count` instances of `instance` before emitting them, to avoid reallocations.

syncGPU.haxe_doc: With the `ManualEmitGPU` flag: runs the `syncShader` on all the instances.

emitGPU.haxe_doc: With the `ManualEmitGPU` flag: runs the compute passes culling the instances and building the draw commands.

dump.haxe_doc: Writes a text report of the primitives, models and instances of the batcher to the file `path` (debug).

class.haxe_doc:
A GPU driven renderer for very large numbers of static instances of many different models.
Register each model once with `addInstance`, then add as many instances as needed with `emitInstance`. Instances are kept from frame to frame: they stay until their group is removed (see `createGroup`). The culling (frustum, distance and optionally occlusion with `hzbCulling`) and the level of detail selection are done on the GPU by compute shaders, and the instances are drawn with indirect draw calls, with all the meshes of the same vertex format in a single primitive.
Requires a driver supporting bindless resources (throws otherwise).

Base class of the compute shaders updating the instance transforms on the GPU (see `Batcher.syncShader`). It provides `getModelView` and `fillModelView` to read and write the transform of an instance.

instanceStride.haxe_doc: The number of 4-floats vectors per instance in `instancesData`.

modelViewOffset.haxe_doc: The offset of the transform matrix in the data of an instance.

syncIDs.haxe_doc: The sync IDs of the instances, given to `Batcher.emitInstance`.

hasSyncIDs.haxe_doc: Tells if the shader uses the sync IDs.

class.haxe_doc: The parameters of a `Batcher.syncShader`, filled by the batcher before running it. Implemented by shaders extending `BaseSync`.
Batcher Implementation

is3D.haxe_doc: Setting is3D to true will switch from a screen space line (constant size whatever the distance) to a world space line

clear.haxe_doc: Removes all the lines drawn so far.

setColorF.haxe_doc: Sets the color of the next lines with float components, from `0` to `1`.

drawLine.haxe_doc: Draws a single line from `p1` to `p2`.

moveTo.haxe_doc: Moves the pen to the given local position without drawing. With `is3D`, it also ends the current polyline.

lineTo.haxe_doc: Draws a line from the pen position to the given local position, and moves the pen there.

color.haxe_doc: The line color, in `0xRRGGBB` format. Changes are applied the next time the bounds change.

bounds.haxe_doc: The box bounds, in local space. If `null`, a unit box centered on the origin (from -0.5 to 0.5) is drawn.

thickness.haxe_doc: The line thickness. Changes are applied the next time the bounds change.

class.haxe_doc:
A debug wireframe box, drawn with 12 lines.
The lines are rebuilt automatically during sync whenever `bounds` changes. It has no collider and is meant for visualizing bounds; use `h3d.prim.Cube` with a `Mesh` for a solid box.

getCameraControllersClass.haxe_doc: Returns the available controller classes (used by editors to let the user pick one).

getCameraControllerClassIdx.haxe_doc: Returns the index of the class of `ctrl` in `getCameraControllersClass()`, or `-1`.

distance.haxe_doc: The current distance between the camera and its target.

targetDistance.haxe_doc: The distance the camera is moving to.

theta.haxe_doc: The current horizontal angle of the camera around the target, in radians.

phi.haxe_doc: The current vertical angle of the camera, in radians, from `0` (looking down from above) to `PI` (looking up from below).

fovY.haxe_doc: The current vertical field of view, in degrees.

target.haxe_doc: The current position the camera is looking at.

minDistance.haxe_doc: The minimum distance reachable by zooming.

maxDistance.haxe_doc: The maximum distance reachable by zooming.

enableZoom.haxe_doc: If `true`, the mouse wheel changes the distance to the target. Otherwise it moves the camera forward and backward.

zoomAmount.haxe_doc: The distance multiplier applied for each mouse wheel step.

friction.haxe_doc: The inertia damping of rotations, between `0` (rotation keeps going) and `1` (stops immediately).

smooth.haxe_doc: The smoothing of the camera movement, between `0` (immediate) and `1` (never reaches the target).

lockZPlanes.haxe_doc: If `false`, the camera `zNear` and `zFar` are adjusted to the distance to the target.

wantedFOV.haxe_doc: The vertical field of view, in degrees, applied by `OrbitCameraController` and `FPSCameraController` every frame.

moveSpeed.haxe_doc: The speed of the keyboard movements.

set.haxe_doc: Set the controller parameters. Distance is ray distance from target. Theta and Phi are the two spherical angles Target is the target position

loadFromCamera.haxe_doc: Load current position from current camera position and target. Call if you want to modify manually the camera.

initFromScene.haxe_doc: Initialize to look at the whole scene, based on reported scene bounds.

toTarget.haxe_doc: Stop animation by directly moving to end position. Call after set() if you don't want to animate the change

onCustomEvent.haxe_doc: Called for each scene event before the controller handles it. Set `e.propagate = false` to prevent the controller from handling the event.

onClick.haxe_doc: Called when the user clicks (presses and releases quickly without moving) with the button used to move the camera.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a controller. It must be added to the scene (directly or through `parent`) to control its camera. @param distance The initial distance to the target.

class.haxe_doc:
Base class of the mouse/keyboard camera controllers. Add a controller to the scene to drive `Scene.camera`: it listens to the scene events and moves the camera smoothly towards the wanted position every frame.
The camera position is expressed in spherical coordinates around `target`: `distance`, `theta` (horizontal angle) and `phi` (vertical angle, from the Z axis). Use `set` to change them and `loadFromCamera` to start from the current camera. See `OrbitCameraController` and `FPSCameraController`.

zNear.haxe_doc: The camera near plane distance, applied every frame.

zFar.haxe_doc: The camera far plane distance, applied every frame.

color.haxe_doc: The line color, in `0xRRGGBB` format. Changes are applied the next time `radius` or `length` is set.

radius.haxe_doc: The capsule radius. Setting it redraws the lines.

length.haxe_doc: The length of the cylindrical part along the X axis, excluding the caps. Setting it redraws the lines.

class.haxe_doc:
A debug wireframe capsule aligned on the X axis: a cylinder of `length` capped by two half spheres of `radius`.
It has no collider and is meant for visualizing capsule colliders (see `h3d.col.Capsule`).
