description.haxe_doc: A human readable description of the plugin.

filename.haxe_doc: The filename of the plugin file.

name.haxe_doc: The name of the plugin.

length.haxe_doc: The number of plugins in the array.

pointerId.haxe_doc: A unique identifier for the pointer causing the event.

width.haxe_doc: The width (magnitude on the X axis), in CSS pixels, of the contact geometry of the pointer.

height.haxe_doc: The height (magnitude on the Y axis), in CSS pixels, of the contact geometry of the pointer.

pressure.haxe_doc: The normalized pressure of the pointer input in the range 0 to 1, where 0 and 1 represent the minimum and maximum pressure the hardware is capable of detecting, respectively.

tangentialPressure.haxe_doc: The normalized tangential pressure of the pointer input (also known as barrel pressure or cylinder stress) in the range -1 to 1, where 0 is the neutral position of the control.

tiltX.haxe_doc: The plane angle (in degrees, in the range of -90 to 90) between the Y-Z plane and the plane containing both the transducer (e.g. pen stylus) axis and the Y axis.

tiltY.haxe_doc: The plane angle (in degrees, in the range of -90 to 90) between the X-Z plane and the plane containing both the transducer (e.g. pen stylus) axis and the X axis.

twist.haxe_doc: The clockwise rotation of the transducer (e.g. pen stylus) around its major axis in degrees, with a value in the range 0 to 359.

pointerType.haxe_doc: Indicates the device type that caused the event (mouse, pen, touch, etc.)

isPrimary.haxe_doc: Indicates if the pointer represents the primary pointer of this pointer type.

getCoalescedEvents.haxe_doc: Returns a sequence of all `PointerEvent` instances that were coalesced into the dispatched `pointermove` event.

timestamp.haxe_doc: Returns a `DOMTimeStamp` representing the time at which the location was retrieved.

coords.haxe_doc: Returns a `Coordinates` object defining the current location.

code.haxe_doc:
Returns an unsigned short representing the error code. The following values are possible: Value Associated constant Description
1 PERMISSION_DENIED The acquisition of the geolocation information failed because the page didn't have the permission to do it.
2 POSITION_UNAVAILABLE The acquisition of the geolocation failed because at least one internal source of position returned an internal error.
3 TIMEOUT The time allowed to acquire the geolocation, defined by PositionOptions.timeout information was reached before the information was obtained.

message.haxe_doc: Returns a human-readable `DOMString` describing the details of the error. Specifications note that this is primarily intended for debugging use and not to be shown directly in a user interface.

timeout.haxe_doc: Is a positive `long` value representing the maximum length of time (in milliseconds) the device is allowed to take in order to return a position. The default value is `Infinity`, meaning that `getCurrentPosition()` won't return until the position is available.

maximumAge.haxe_doc: Is a positive `long` value indicating the maximum age in milliseconds of a possible cached position that is acceptable to return. If set to `0`, it means that the device cannot use a cached position and must attempt to retrieve the real current position. If set to `Infinity` the device must return a cached position regardless of its age. Default: 0.

enableHighAccuracy.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` that indicates the application would like to receive the best possible results. If `true` and if the device is able to provide a more accurate position, it will do so. Note that this can result in slower response times or increased power consumption (with a GPS chip on a mobile device for example). On the other hand, if `false`, the device can take the liberty to save resources by responding more quickly and/or using less power. Default: `false`.

width.haxe_doc: Is a `long` value reflecting the obsolete `width` attribute, containing a fixed-size length for the `pre` element.

value.haxe_doc: Is a `double` value that reflects the current value; if the progress bar is an indeterminate progress bar, it returns `0`.

max.haxe_doc: Is a `double` value reflecting the content attribute of the same name, limited to numbers greater than zero. Its default value is `1.0`.

position.haxe_doc: Returns a `double` value returning the result of dividing the current value (`value`) by the maximum value (`max`); if the progress bar is an indeterminate progress bar, it returns `-1`.

labels.haxe_doc: Returns `NodeList` containing the list of `label` elements that are labels for this element.

cite.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` reflecting the `cite` HTML attribute, containing a URL for the source of the quotation.

startContainer.haxe_doc: Returns the `Node` within which the `Range` starts.

startOffset.haxe_doc: Returns a number representing where in the `startContainer` the `Range` starts.

endContainer.haxe_doc: Returns the `Node` within which the `Range` ends.

endOffset.haxe_doc: Returns a number representing where in the `endContainer` the `Range` ends.

collapsed.haxe_doc: Returns a `Boolean` indicating whether the range's start and end points are at the same position.

commonAncestorContainer.haxe_doc: Returns the deepest `Node` that contains the `startContainer` and `endContainer` nodes.

setStart.haxe_doc: Sets the start position of a `Range`. @throws DOMError

setEnd.haxe_doc: Sets the end position of a `Range`. @throws DOMError

setStartBefore.haxe_doc: Sets the start position of a `Range` relative to another `Node`. @throws DOMError

setStartAfter.haxe_doc: Sets the start position of a `Range` relative to another `Node`. @throws DOMError

setEndBefore.haxe_doc: Sets the end position of a `Range` relative to another `Node`. @throws DOMError

setEndAfter.haxe_doc: Sets the end position of a `Range` relative to another `Node`. @throws DOMError

collapse.haxe_doc: Collapses the `Range` to one of its boundary points.

selectNode.haxe_doc: Sets the `Range` to contain the `Node` and its contents. @throws DOMError

selectNodeContents.haxe_doc: Sets the `Range` to contain the contents of a `Node`. @throws DOMError

compareBoundaryPoints.haxe_doc: Compares the boundary points of the `Range` with another `Range`. @throws DOMError

deleteContents.haxe_doc: Removes the contents of a `Range` from the `Document`. @throws DOMError

extractContents.haxe_doc: Moves contents of a `Range` from the document tree into a `DocumentFragment`. @throws DOMError

cloneContents.haxe_doc: Returns a `DocumentFragment` copying the nodes of a `Range`. @throws DOMError

insertNode.haxe_doc: Insert a `Node` at the start of a `Range`. @throws DOMError

surroundContents.haxe_doc: Moves content of a `Range` into a new `Node`. @throws DOMError

cloneRange.haxe_doc: Returns a `Range` object with boundary points identical to the cloned `Range`.

detach.haxe_doc: Releases the `Range` from use to improve performance.

isPointInRange.haxe_doc: Returns a `boolean` indicating whether the given point is in the `Range`. @throws DOMError

comparePoint.haxe_doc: Returns -1, 0, or 1 indicating whether the point occurs before, inside, or after the `Range`. @throws DOMError

intersectsNode.haxe_doc: Returns a `boolean` indicating whether the given node intersects the `Range`. @throws DOMError

createContextualFragment.haxe_doc: Returns a `DocumentFragment` created from a given string of code. @throws DOMError

getClientRects.haxe_doc: Returns a list of `DOMRect` objects that aggregates the results of `Element.getClientRects()` for all the elements in the `Range`.

getBoundingClientRect.haxe_doc: Returns a `DOMRect` object which bounds the entire contents of the `Range`; this would be the union of all the rectangles returned by `range.getClientRects()`.

url.haxe_doc: Contains the URL of the request.

headers.haxe_doc: Contains the associated `Headers` object of the request.

destination.haxe_doc: Returns a string from the `RequestDestination` enum describing the request's destination. This is a string indicating the type of content being requested.

referrer.haxe_doc: Contains the referrer of the request (e.g., `client`).

referrerPolicy.haxe_doc: Contains the referrer policy of the request (e.g., `no-referrer`).

mode.haxe_doc: Contains the mode of the request (e.g., `cors`, `no-cors`, `same-origin`, `navigate`.)

credentials.haxe_doc: Contains the credentials of the request (e.g., `"omit"`, `"same-origin"`, `"include"`). The default is `"same-origin"`.

cache.haxe_doc: Contains the cache mode of the request (e.g., `default`, `reload`, `no-cache`).

redirect.haxe_doc: Contains the mode for how redirects are handled. It may be one of `follow`, `error`, or `manual`.

integrity.haxe_doc: Contains the subresource integrity value of the request (e.g., `sha256-BpfBw7ivV8q2jLiT13fxDYAe2tJllusRSZ273h2nFSE=`).

clone.haxe_doc: Creates a copy of the current `Request` object. @throws DOMError

error.haxe_doc: Returns a new `Response` object associated with a network error.

redirect.haxe_doc: Creates a new response with a different URL. @throws DOMError

type.haxe_doc: Contains the type of the response (e.g., `basic`, `cors`).

url.haxe_doc: Contains the URL of the response.

redirected.haxe_doc: Indicates whether or not the response is the result of a redirect; that is, its URL list has more than one entry.

status.haxe_doc: Contains the status code of the response (e.g., `200` for a success).

ok.haxe_doc: Contains a boolean stating whether the response was successful (status in the range 200-299) or not.

statusText.haxe_doc: Contains the status message corresponding to the status code (e.g., `OK` for `200`).

headers.haxe_doc: Contains the `Headers` object associated with the response.

clone.haxe_doc: Creates a clone of a `Response` object. @throws DOMError

type.haxe_doc: Returns the document's current orientation type, one of "portrait-primary", "portrait-secondary", "landscape-primary", or "landscape-secondary".

angle.haxe_doc: Returns the document's current orientation angle.

onchange.haxe_doc: Fired whenever is the `EventHandler` called when the screen changes orientation.

lock.haxe_doc: Locks the orientation of the containing document to its default orientation and returns a `Promise`. @throws DOMError

unlock.haxe_doc: Unlocks the orientation of the containing document from its default orientation. @throws DOMError

autofocus.haxe_doc: A `Boolean` reflecting the `autofocus` HTML attribute, which indicates whether the control should have input focus when the page loads, unless the user overrides it, for example by typing in a different control. Only one form-associated element in a document can have this attribute specified. `2.0`

disabled.haxe_doc: A `Boolean` reflecting the `disabled` HTML attribute, which indicates whether the control is disabled. If it is disabled, it does not accept clicks.

form.haxe_doc: An `HTMLFormElement` referencing the form that this element is associated with. If the element is not associated with of a `form` element, then it returns `null`.

multiple.haxe_doc: A `Boolean` reflecting the `multiple` HTML attribute, which indicates whether multiple items can be selected.

name.haxe_doc: A `DOMString` reflecting the `name` HTML attribute, containing the name of this control used by servers and DOM search functions.

required.haxe_doc: A `Boolean` reflecting the `required` HTML attribute, which indicates whether the user is required to select a value before submitting the form. `2.0`

size.haxe_doc: A `long` reflecting the `size` HTML attribute, which contains the number of visible items in the control. The default is 1, unless `multiple` is true, in which case it is 4.

type.haxe_doc: A `DOMString` represeting the form control's type. When `multiple` is `true`, it returns `"select-multiple"`; otherwise, it returns `"select-one"`.

options.haxe_doc: An `HTMLOptionsCollection` representing the set of `option` elements contained by this element.

length.haxe_doc: An `unsigned long `The number of `option` elements in this `select` element.

selectedOptions.haxe_doc: An `HTMLCollection` representing the set of `option` elements that are selected.

selectedIndex.haxe_doc: A `long` reflecting the index of the first selected `option` element. The value `-1` indicates no element is selected.

value.haxe_doc: A `DOMString` reflecting the value of the form control (the first selected option). Returns the value attribute of the option element or if it is missing, the text attribute.

willValidate.haxe_doc: A `Boolean` that indicates whether the button is a candidate for constraint validation. It is false if any conditions bar it from constraint validation.

validity.haxe_doc: A `ValidityState` reflecting the validity state that this control is in.

validationMessage.haxe_doc: A `DOMString` representing a localized message that describes the validation constraints that the control does not satisfy (if any). This attribute is the empty string if the control is not a candidate for constraint validation (`willValidate` is false), or it satisfies its constraints.

labels.haxe_doc: A `NodeList` of `label` elements associated with the element.

item.haxe_doc: Gets an item from the options collection for this `select` element. You can also access an item by specifying the index in array-style brackets or parentheses, without calling this method explicitly.

namedItem.haxe_doc: Gets the item in the options collection with the specified name. The name string can match either the `id` or the `name` attribute of an option node. You can also access an item by specifying the name in array-style brackets or parentheses, without calling this method explicitly.

add.haxe_doc: Adds an element to the collection of `option` elements for this `select` element. @throws DOMError

remove.haxe_doc: Removes the element at the specified index from the options collection for this select element.
Removes the element at the specified index from the options collection for this select element.

checkValidity.haxe_doc: Checks whether the element has any constraints and whether it satisfies them. If the element fails its constraints, the browser fires a cancelable `invalid` event at the element (and returns `false`).

setCustomValidity.haxe_doc: Sets the custom validity message for the selection element to the specified message. Use the empty string to indicate that the element does not have a custom validity error.

anchorNode.haxe_doc: Returns the `Node` in which the selection begins.

anchorOffset.haxe_doc: Returns a number representing the offset of the selection's anchor within the anchorNode. If anchorNode is a text node, this is the number of characters within anchorNode preceding the anchor. If anchorNode is an element, this is the number of child nodes of the anchorNode preceding the anchor.

focusNode.haxe_doc: Returns the `Node` in which the selection ends.

focusOffset.haxe_doc: Returns a number representing the offset of the selection's anchor within the focusNode. If focusNode is a text node, this is the number of characters within focusNode preceding the focus. If focusNode is an element, this is the number of child nodes of the focusNode preceding the focus.

isCollapsed.haxe_doc: Returns a Boolean indicating whether the selection's start and end points are at the same position.

rangeCount.haxe_doc: Returns the number of ranges in the selection.

type.haxe_doc: Returns a `DOMString` describing the type of the current selection.

getRangeAt.haxe_doc: Returns a `Range` object representing one of the ranges currently selected. @throws DOMError

addRange.haxe_doc: A `Range` object that will be added to the selection. @throws DOMError

removeRange.haxe_doc: Removes a range from the selection. @throws DOMError

removeAllRanges.haxe_doc: Removes all ranges from the selection. @throws DOMError

collapse.haxe_doc: Collapses the current selection to a single point. @throws DOMError

collapseToStart.haxe_doc: Collapses the selection to the start of the first range in the selection. @throws DOMError

collapseToEnd.haxe_doc: Collapses the selection to the end of the last range in the selection. @throws DOMError

extend.haxe_doc: Moves the focus of the selection to a specified point. @throws DOMError

setBaseAndExtent.haxe_doc: Sets the selection to be a range including all or parts of two specified DOM nodes, and any content located between them. @throws DOMError

selectAllChildren.haxe_doc: Adds all the children of the specified node to the selection. @throws DOMError

deleteFromDocument.haxe_doc: Deletes the selection's content from the document. @throws DOMError

containsNode.haxe_doc: Indicates if a certain node is part of the selection. @throws DOMError

scriptURL.haxe_doc: Returns the `ServiceWorker` serialized script URL defined as part of `ServiceWorkerRegistration`. The URL must be on the same origin as the document that registers the `ServiceWorker`.

state.haxe_doc: Returns the state of the service worker. It returns one of the following values: `installing`, `installed,` `activating`, `activated`, or `redundant`.

onstatechange.haxe_doc: An `EventListener` property called whenever an event of type `statechange` is fired; it is basically fired anytime the `ServiceWorker.state` changes.

controller.haxe_doc: Returns a `ServiceWorker` object if its state is `activated` (the same object returned by `ServiceWorkerRegistration.active`). This property returns `null` during a force-refresh request (Shift + refresh) or if there is no active worker.

ready.haxe_doc: Provides a way of delaying code execution until a service worker is active. It returns a `Promise` that will never reject, and which waits indefinitely until the `ServiceWorkerRegistration` associated with the current page has an `ServiceWorkerRegistration.active` worker. Once that condition is met, it resolves with the `ServiceWorkerRegistration`.

oncontrollerchange.haxe_doc: Fired whenever a `controllerchange` event occurs — when the document's associated `ServiceWorkerRegistration` acquires a new `ServiceWorkerRegistration.active` worker.

onerror.haxe_doc: Fired whenever an `error` event occurs in the associated service workers.

onmessage.haxe_doc: Fired whenever a `message` event occurs — when incoming messages are received to the `ServiceWorkerContainer` object (e.g. via a `MessagePort.postMessage()` call.)

getRegistration.haxe_doc: Gets a `ServiceWorkerRegistration` object whose scope matches the provided document URL. If the method can't return a `ServiceWorkerRegistration`, it returns a `Promise`.

getRegistrations.haxe_doc: Returns all `ServiceWorkerRegistration` objects associated with a `ServiceWorkerContainer` in an array. If the method can't return `ServiceWorkerRegistration` objects, it returns a `Promise`.

installing.haxe_doc: Returns a service worker whose state is `installing`. This is initially set to `null`.

waiting.haxe_doc: Returns a service worker whose state is `waiting`. This is initially set to `null`.

active.haxe_doc: Returns a service worker whose state is either `activating` or `activated`. This is initially set to `null`. An active worker will control a `ServiceWorkerClient` if the client's URL falls within the scope of the registration (the `scope` option set when `ServiceWorkerContainer.register` is first called.)

scope.haxe_doc: Returns a unique identifier for a service worker registration. This must be on the same origin as the document that registers the `ServiceWorker`.

onupdatefound.haxe_doc: An `EventListener` property called whenever an event of type `updatefound` is fired; it is fired any time the `ServiceWorkerRegistration.installing` property acquires a new service worker.

pushManager.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the `PushManager` interface for managing push subscriptions including subscribing, getting an active subscription, and accessing push permission status.

update.haxe_doc: Checks the server for an updated version of the service worker without consulting caches. @throws DOMError

unregister.haxe_doc: Unregisters the service worker registration and returns a `Promise`. The service worker will finish any ongoing operations before it is unregistered. @throws DOMError

showNotification.haxe_doc: Displays the notification with the requested title. @throws DOMError

getNotifications.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` that resolves to an array of `Notification` objects. @throws DOMError

mode.haxe_doc: The mode of the `ShadowRoot` — either `open` or `closed`. This defines whether or not the shadow root's internal features are accessible from JavaScript.

host.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the DOM element the `ShadowRoot` is attached to.

innerHTML.haxe_doc: Sets or returns a reference to the DOM tree inside the `ShadowRoot`.

name.haxe_doc: `DOMString`: Can be used to get and set the slot's name.

assignedNodes.haxe_doc: Returns the sequence of elements assigned to this slot, or alternatively the slot's fallback content.

mode.haxe_doc: Controls how the order of media segments in the `SourceBuffer` is handled, in terms of whether they can be appended in any order, or they have to be kept in a strict sequence.

updating.haxe_doc: A boolean indicating whether the `SourceBuffer` is currently being updated — i.e. whether an `SourceBuffer.appendBuffer()`, `SourceBuffer.appendStream()`, or `SourceBuffer.remove()` operation is currently in progress.

buffered.haxe_doc: Returns the time ranges that are currently buffered in the `SourceBuffer`.

timestampOffset.haxe_doc: Controls the offset applied to timestamps inside media segments that are subsequently appended to the `SourceBuffer`.

appendWindowStart.haxe_doc: Controls the timestamp for the start of the append window. This is a timestamp range that can be used to filter what media data is appended to the `SourceBuffer`. Coded media frames with timestamps within this range will be appended, whereas those outside the range will be filtered out.

appendWindowEnd.haxe_doc: Controls the timestamp for the end of the append window.

onupdatestart.haxe_doc: Fired whenever the value of `SourceBuffer.updating` transitions from `false` to `true`.

onupdate.haxe_doc: Fired whenever `SourceBuffer.appendBuffer()` method or the `SourceBuffer.remove()` completes. `SourceBuffer.updating` changes from `true` to `false`. This event is fired before `onupdateend`.

onupdateend.haxe_doc: Fired whenever `SourceBuffer.appendBuffer()` method or the `SourceBuffer.remove()` has ended. This event is fired after `onupdate`.

onerror.haxe_doc: Fired whenever an error occurs during `SourceBuffer.appendBuffer()` or `SourceBuffer.appendStream()`. `SourceBuffer.updating` changes from `true` to `false`.

onabort.haxe_doc: Fired whenever `SourceBuffer.appendBuffer()` or `SourceBuffer.appendStream()` is ended by a call to `SourceBuffer.abort()`. `SourceBuffer.updating` changes from `true` to `false`.

appendBuffer.haxe_doc: Appends media segment data from an `ArrayBuffer` or `ArrayBufferView` object to the `SourceBuffer`. @throws DOMError
Appends media segment data from an `ArrayBuffer` or `ArrayBufferView` object to the `SourceBuffer`. @throws DOMError

abort.haxe_doc: Aborts the current segment and resets the segment parser. @throws DOMError

remove.haxe_doc: Removes media segments within a specific time range from the `SourceBuffer`. @throws DOMError

changeType.haxe_doc: Changes the `MIME type` that future calls to `SourceBuffer.appendBuffer` will expect the new data to conform to. @throws DOMError

length.haxe_doc: Returns the number of `SourceBuffer` objects in the list.

onaddsourcebuffer.haxe_doc: The event handler for the `addsourcebuffer` event.

onremovesourcebuffer.haxe_doc: The event handler for the `removesourcebuffer` event.

src.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` reflecting the `src` HTML attribute, containing the URL for the media resource. The `HTMLSourceElement.src` property has a meaning only when the associated `source` element is nested in a media element that is a `video` or an `audio` element. It has no meaning and is ignored when it is nested in a `picture` element. Note: If the `src` property is updated (along with any siblings), the parent `HTMLMediaElement`'s `load` method should be called when done, since `source` elements are not re-scanned automatically.

type.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` reflecting the `type` HTML attribute, containing the type of the media resource.

srcset.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` reflecting the `srcset` HTML attribute, containing a list of candidate images, separated by a comma (`',', U+002C COMMA`). A candidate image is a URL followed by a `'w'` with the width of the images, or an `'x'` followed by the pixel density.

sizes.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` representing image sizes between breakpoints

media.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` reflecting the `media` HTML attribute, containing the intended type of the media resource.

pending.haxe_doc: A `Boolean` that returns `true` if the utterance queue contains as-yet-unspoken utterances.

speaking.haxe_doc: A `Boolean` that returns `true` if an utterance is currently in the process of being spoken — even if `SpeechSynthesis` is in a paused state.

paused.haxe_doc: A `Boolean` that returns `true` if the `SpeechSynthesis` object is in a paused state.

onvoiceschanged.haxe_doc: Fired when the list of `SpeechSynthesisVoice` objects that would be returned by the `SpeechSynthesis.getVoices()` method has changed.

speak.haxe_doc: Adds an `SpeechSynthesisUtterance` to the utterance queue; it will be spoken when any other utterances queued before it have been spoken.

cancel.haxe_doc: Removes all utterances from the utterance queue.

pause.haxe_doc: Puts the `SpeechSynthesis` object into a paused state.

resume.haxe_doc: Puts the `SpeechSynthesis` object into a non-paused state: resumes it if it was already paused.

getVoices.haxe_doc: Returns a list of `SpeechSynthesisVoice` objects representing all the available voices on the current device.

text.haxe_doc: Gets and sets the text that will be synthesised when the utterance is spoken.

lang.haxe_doc: Gets and sets the language of the utterance.

voice.haxe_doc: Gets and sets the voice that will be used to speak the utterance.

volume.haxe_doc: Gets and sets the volume that the utterance will be spoken at.

rate.haxe_doc: Gets and sets the speed at which the utterance will be spoken at.

pitch.haxe_doc: Gets and sets the pitch at which the utterance will be spoken at.

onstart.haxe_doc: Fired when the utterance has begun to be spoken.

onend.haxe_doc: Fired when the utterance has finished being spoken.

onerror.haxe_doc: Fired when an error occurs that prevents the utterance from being succesfully spoken.

onpause.haxe_doc: Fired when the utterance is paused part way through.

onresume.haxe_doc: Fired when a paused utterance is resumed.

onmark.haxe_doc: Fired when the spoken utterance reaches a named SSML "mark" tag.

onboundary.haxe_doc: Fired when the spoken utterance reaches a word or sentence boundary.

voiceURI.haxe_doc: Returns the type of URI and location of the speech synthesis service for this voice.

name.haxe_doc: Returns a human-readable name that represents the voice.

lang.haxe_doc: Returns a BCP 47 language tag indicating the language of the voice.

localService.haxe_doc: A `Boolean` indicating whether the voice is supplied by a local speech synthesizer service (`true`), or a remote speech synthesizer service (`false`.)

default_.haxe_doc: A `Boolean` indicating whether the voice is the default voice for the current app language (`true`), or not (`false`.)

length.haxe_doc: Returns an integer representing the number of data items stored in the `Storage` object.

key.haxe_doc: When passed a number n, this method will return the name of the nth key in the storage. @throws DOMError

getItem.haxe_doc: When passed a key name, will return that key's value. @throws DOMError

setItem.haxe_doc: When passed a key name and value, will add that key to the storage, or update that key's value if it already exists. @throws DOMError

removeItem.haxe_doc: When passed a key name, will remove that key from the storage. @throws DOMError

clear.haxe_doc: When invoked, will empty all keys out of the storage. @throws DOMError

usage.haxe_doc: A numeric value approximating the amount of storage space currently being used by the site or Web app, out of the available space as indicated by `quota`.

quota.haxe_doc: A numeric value which provides a conservative approximation of the total storage the user's device or computer has available for the site origin or Web app. It's possible that there's more than this amount of space available though you can't rely on that being the case.

persisted.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` that resolves to `true` if persistence has already been granted for your site's storage. @throws DOMError

persist.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` that resolves to `true` if the user agent is able to persist your site's storage. @throws DOMError

estimate.haxe_doc: Returns a `StorageEstimate` object containing usage and quota numbers for your origin. @throws DOMError

disabled.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` value representing whether or not the stylesheet is disabled (true) or not (false).

media.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` representing the intended destination medium for style information.

type.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` representing the type of style being applied by this statement.

encrypt.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` of the encrypted data corresponding to the clear text, algorithm and key given as parameters. @throws DOMError

decrypt.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` of the clear data corresponding to the encrypted text, algorithm and key given as parameters. @throws DOMError

sign.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` of the signature corresponding to the text, algorithm and key given as parameters. @throws DOMError

verify.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` of a `Boolean` value indicating if the signature given as parameter matches the text, algorithm and key also given as parameters. @throws DOMError

digest.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` of a digest generated from the algorithm and text given as parameters. @throws DOMError

generateKey.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` of a newly generated `CryptoKey`, for symmetrical algorithms, or a `CryptoKeyPair`, containing two newly generated keys, for asymmetrical algorithm, that matches the algorithm, the usages and the extractability given as parameters. @throws DOMError

Returns a `Promise` of a newly generated `CryptoKey`, for symmetrical algorithms, or a `CryptoKeyPair`, containing two newly generated keys, for asymmetrical algorithm, that matches the algorithm, the usages and the extractability given as parameters. @throws DOMError

deriveKey.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` of a newly generated `CryptoKey` derived from a master key and a specific algorithm given as parameters. @throws DOMError

deriveBits.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` of a newly generated buffer of pseudo-random bits derived from a master key and a specific algorithm given as parameters. @throws DOMError
Returns a `Promise` of a newly generated buffer of pseudo-random bits derived from a master key and a specific algorithm given as parameters. @throws DOMError

importKey.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` of a `CryptoKey` corresponding to the format, the algorithm, the raw key data, the usages and the extractability given as parameters. @throws DOMError
Returns a `Promise` of a `CryptoKey` corresponding to the format, the algorithm, the raw key data, the usages and the extractability given as parameters. @throws DOMError

exportKey.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` of a buffer containing the key in the format requested. @throws DOMError

wrapKey.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` of a wrapped symmetric key for usage (transfer, storage) in insecure environments. The wrapped buffer returned is in the format given in parameters, and contains the key wrapped by the given wrapping key with the given algorithm. @throws DOMError

Returns a `Promise` of a wrapped symmetric key for usage (transfer, storage) in insecure environments. The wrapped buffer returned is in the format given in parameters, and contains the key wrapped by the given wrapping key with the given algorithm. @throws DOMError

unwrapKey.haxe_doc: Returns a `Promise` of a `CryptoKey` corresponding to the wrapped key given in parameter. @throws DOMError

align.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` which represents an enumerated attribute indicating alignment of the caption with respect to the table.

colSpan.haxe_doc: An unsigned long integer indicating the number of columns this cell must span; this lets the cell occupy space across multiple columns of the table. It reflects the `colspan` attribute.

rowSpan.haxe_doc: An unsigned long integer indicating the number of rows this cell must span; this lets a cell occupy space across multiple rows of the table. It reflects the `rowspan` attribute.

headers.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMSettableTokenList` describing a list of `id` of `th` elements that represents headers associated with the cell. It reflects the `headers` attribute.

cellIndex.haxe_doc: A long integer representing the cell's position in the `HTMLTableRowElement.cells` collection of the `tr` the cell is contained within. If the cell doesn't belong to a `tr`, it returns `-1`.

abbr.haxe_doc: A `DOMString` which can be used on `th` elements (not on `td`), specifying an alternative label for the header cell.. This alternate label can be used in other contexts, such as when describing the headers that apply to a data cell. This is used to offer a shorter term for use by screen readers in particular, and is a valuable accessibility tool. Usually the value of `abbr` is an abbreviation or acronym, but can be any text that's appropriate contextually.

caption.haxe_doc: Is a `HTMLTableCaptionElement` representing the first `caption` that is a child of the element, or `null` if none is found. When set, if the object doesn't represent a `caption`, a `DOMException` with the `HierarchyRequestError` name is thrown. If a correct object is given, it is inserted in the tree as the first child of this element and the first `caption` that is a child of this element is removed from the tree, if any.

tHead.haxe_doc: Is a `HTMLTableSectionElement` representing the first `thead` that is a child of the element, or `null` if none is found. When set, if the object doesn't represent a `thead`, a `DOMException` with the `HierarchyRequestError` name is thrown. If a correct object is given, it is inserted in the tree immediately before the first element that is neither a `caption`, nor a `colgroup`, or as the last child if there is no such element, and the first `thead` that is a child of this element is removed from the tree, if any.

tFoot.haxe_doc: Is a `HTMLTableSectionElement` representing the first `tfoot` that is a child of the element, or `null` if none is found. When set, if the object doesn't represent a `tfoot`, a `DOMException` with the `HierarchyRequestError` name is thrown. If a correct object is given, it is inserted in the tree immediately before the first element that is neither a `caption`, a `colgroup`, nor a `thead`, or as the last child if there is no such element, and the first `tfoot` that is a child of this element is removed from the tree, if any.

tBodies.haxe_doc: Returns a live `HTMLCollection` containing all the `tbody` of the element. The `HTMLCollection` is live and is automatically updated when the `HTMLTableElement` changes.

rows.haxe_doc: Returns a live `HTMLCollection` containing all the rows of the element, that is all `tr` that are a child of the element, or a child or one of its `thead`, `tbody` and `tfoot` children. The rows members of a `thead` appear first, in tree order, and those members of a `tbody` last, also in tree order. The `HTMLCollection` is live and is automatically updated when the `HTMLTableElement` changes.

align.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing an enumerated value reflecting the `align` attribute. It indicates the alignment of the element's contents with respect to the surrounding context. The possible values are `"left"`, `"right"`, and `"center"`.

border.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the width in pixels of the border of the table. It reflects the obsolete `border` attribute.

frame.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the type of the external borders of the table. It reflects the obsolete `frame` attribute and can take one of the following values: `"void"`, `"above"`, `"below"`, `"hsides"`, `"vsides"`, `"lhs"`, `"rhs"`, `"box"`, or `"border"`.

rules.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the type of the internal borders of the table. It reflects the obsolete `rules` attribute and can take one of the following values: `"none"`, `"groups"`, `"rows"`, `"cols"`, or `"all"`.

summary.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing a description of the purpose or the structure of the table. It reflects the obsolete `summary` attribute.

width.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the length in pixels or in percentage of the desired width fo the entire table. It reflects the obsolete `width` attribute.

bgColor.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the background color of the cells. It reflects the obsolete `bgColor` attribute.

cellPadding.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the width in pixels of the horizontal and vertical sapce between cell content and cell borders. It reflects the obsolete `cellpadding` attribute.

cellSpacing.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the width in pixels of the horizontal and vertical separation between cells. It reflects the obsolete `cellspacing` attribute.

createCaption.haxe_doc: Returns an `HTMLElement` representing the first `caption` that is a child of the element. If none is found, a new one is created and inserted in the tree as the first child of the `table` element.

deleteCaption.haxe_doc: Removes the first `caption` that is a child of the element.

createTHead.haxe_doc: Returns an `HTMLElement` representing the first `thead` that is a child of the element. If none is found, a new one is created and inserted in the tree immediately before the first element that is neither a `caption`, nor a `colgroup`, or as the last child if there is no such element.

deleteTHead.haxe_doc: Removes the first `thead` that is a child of the element.

createTFoot.haxe_doc: Returns an `HTMLElement` representing the first `tfoot` that is a child of the element. If none is found, a new one is created and inserted in the tree immediately before the first element that is neither a `caption`, a `colgroup`, nor a `thead`, or as the last child if there is no such element.

deleteTFoot.haxe_doc: Removes the first `tfoot` that is a child of the element.

insertRow.haxe_doc: Returns an `HTMLTableRowElement` representing a new row of the table. It inserts it in the rows collection immediately before the `tr` element at the given `index` position. If necessary a `tbody` is created. If the `index` is `-1`, the new row is appended to the collection. If the `index` is smaller than `-1` or greater than the number of rows in the collection, a `DOMException` with the value `IndexSizeError` is raised. @throws DOMError

deleteRow.haxe_doc: Removes the row corresponding to the `index` given in parameter. If the `index` value is `-1` the last row is removed; if it smaller than `-1` or greater than the amount of rows in the collection, a `DOMException` with the value `IndexSizeError` is raised. @throws DOMError

rowIndex.haxe_doc: Returns a `long` value which gives the logical position of the row within the entire table. If the row is not part of a table, returns `-1`.

sectionRowIndex.haxe_doc: Returns a `long` value which gives the logical position of the row within the table section it belongs to. If the row is not part of a section, returns `-1`.

cells.haxe_doc: Returns a live `HTMLCollection` containing the cells in the row. The `HTMLCollection` is live and is automatically updated when cells are added or removed.

align.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing an enumerated value reflecting the `align` attribute. It indicates the alignment of the element's contents with respect to the surrounding context. The possible values are `"left"`, `"right"`, and `"center"`.

ch.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing one single character. This character is the one to align all the cell of a column on. It reflects the `char` and default to the decimal points associated with the language, e.g. `'.'` for English, or `','` for French. This property was optional and was not very well supported.

chOff.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing a integer indicating how many characters must be left at the right (for left-to-right scripts; or at the left for right-to-left scripts) of the character defined by `HTMLTableRowElement.ch`. This property was optional and was not very well supported.

vAlign.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` representing an enumerated value indicating how the content of the cell must be vertically aligned. It reflects the `valign` attribute and can have one of the following values: `"top"`, `"middle"`, `"bottom"`, or `"baseline"`.

bgColor.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the background color of the cells. It reflects the obsolete `bgColor` attribute.

insertCell.haxe_doc: Inserts a new cell just before the given position in the row. If the given position is not given or is `-1`, it appends the cell to the row. If the given position is greater (or equal as it starts at zero) than the amount of cells in the row, or is smaller than `-1`, it raises a `DOMException` with the `IndexSizeError` value. Returns a reference to a HTMLTableCellElement [en-US]. @throws DOMError

deleteCell.haxe_doc: Removes the cell at the given position in the row. If the given position is greater (or equal as it starts at zero) than the amount of cells in the row, or is smaller than `0`, it raises a `DOMException` with the `IndexSizeError` value. @throws DOMError

rows.haxe_doc: Returns a live `HTMLCollection` containing the rows in the section. The `HTMLCollection` is live and is automatically updated when rows are added or removed.

align.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing an enumerated value reflecting the `align` attribute. It indicates the alignment of the element's contents with respect to the surrounding context. The possible values are `"left"`, `"right"`, and `"center"`.

ch.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing one single chararcter. This character is the one to align all the cell of a column on. It reflects the `char` and default to the decimal points associated with the language, e.g. `'.'` for English, or `','` for French. This property was optional and was not very well supported.

chOff.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing a integer indicating how many characters must be left at the right (for left-to-right scripts; or at the left for right-to-left scripts) of the character defined by `HTMLTableRowElement.ch`. This property was optional and was not very well supported.

vAlign.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` representing an enumerated value indicating how the content of the cell must be vertically aligned. It reflects the `valign` attribute and can have one of the following values: `"top"`, `"middle"`, `"bottom"`, or `"baseline"`.

insertRow.haxe_doc: Inserts a new row just before the given position in the section. If the given position is not given or is `-1`, it appends the row to the end of section. If the given position is greater (or equal as it starts at zero) than the amount of rows in the section, or is smaller than `-1`, it raises a `DOMException` with the `IndexSizeError` value. @throws DOMError

deleteRow.haxe_doc: Removes the cell at the given position in the section. If the given position is greater (or equal as it starts at zero) than the amount of rows in the section, or is smaller than `0`, it raises a `DOMException` with the `IndexSizeError` value. @throws DOMError

width.haxe_doc: Is a `double` giving the calculated width of a segment of inline text in CSS pixels. It takes into account the current font of the context.

kind.haxe_doc: Returns a `DOMString` indicating what kind of text track the `TextTrack` describes. The value must be one of those in the TextTrackKind enum.

label.haxe_doc: A human-readable `DOMString` which contains the text track's label, if one is present; otherwise, this is an empty string (`""`), in which case a custom label may need to be generated by your code using other attributes of the track, if the track's label needs to be exposed to the user.

language.haxe_doc: A `DOMString` which specifies the text language in which the text track's contents is written. The value must adhere to the format specified in the Tags for Identifying Languages (BCP 47) document from the IETF, just like the HTML `lang` attribute. For example, this can be `"en-US"` for United States English or `"pt-BR"` for Brazilian Portuguese.

id.haxe_doc: A `DOMString` which identifies the track, if it has one. If it doesn't have an ID, then this value is an empty string (`""`). If the `TextTrack` is associated with a `track` element, then the track's ID matches the element's ID.

inBandMetadataTrackDispatchType.haxe_doc: Returns a `DOMString` which indicates the track's in-band metadata track dispatch type. needs details

mode.haxe_doc: A `DOMString` specifying the track's current mode. Changing this property's value changes the track's current mode to match. Permitted values are listed under Text track mode constants.

cues.haxe_doc: A `TextTrackCueList` which contains all of the track's cues.

activeCues.haxe_doc: A `TextTrackCueList` object listing the currently active set of text track cues. Track cues are active if the current playback position of the media is between the cues' start and end times.

oncuechange.haxe_doc: A `EventHandler` specifying a function to be called when a `cuechange` event occurs. Handling these events lets you know when cues are entered and exited. A given text cue appears when the cue is entered and disappears when the cue is exited.

length.haxe_doc: Returns an `unsigned long` representing the number of time ranges represented by the time range object.

start.haxe_doc: Returns the time for the start of the range with the specified index. @throws DOMError

end.haxe_doc: Returns the time for the end of the specified range. @throws DOMError

text.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` representing the text of the document's title.

identifier.haxe_doc: Returns a unique identifier for this `Touch` object. A given touch point (say, by a finger) will have the same identifier for the duration of its movement around the surface. This lets you ensure that you're tracking the same touch all the time.

target.haxe_doc: Returns the `Element` on which the touch point started when it was first placed on the surface, even if the touch point has since moved outside the interactive area of that element or even been removed from the document.

screenX.haxe_doc: Returns the X coordinate of the touch point relative to the left edge of the screen.

screenY.haxe_doc: Returns the Y coordinate of the touch point relative to the top edge of the screen.

clientX.haxe_doc: Returns the X coordinate of the touch point relative to the left edge of the browser viewport, not including any scroll offset.

clientY.haxe_doc: Returns the Y coordinate of the touch point relative to the top edge of the browser viewport, not including any scroll offset.

pageX.haxe_doc: Returns the X coordinate of the touch point relative to the left edge of the document. Unlike `clientX`, this value includes the horizontal scroll offset, if any.

pageY.haxe_doc: Returns the Y coordinate of the touch point relative to the top of the document. Unlike `clientY,` this value includes the vertical scroll offset, if any.

radiusX.haxe_doc: Returns the X radius of the ellipse that most closely circumscribes the area of contact with the screen. The value is in pixels of the same scale as `screenX`.

radiusY.haxe_doc: Returns the Y radius of the ellipse that most closely circumscribes the area of contact with the screen. The value is in pixels of the same scale as `screenY`.

rotationAngle.haxe_doc: Returns the angle (in degrees) that the ellipse described by radiusX and radiusY must be rotated, clockwise, to most accurately cover the area of contact between the user and the surface.

force.haxe_doc: Returns the amount of pressure being applied to the surface by the user, as a `float` between `0.0` (no pressure) and `1.0` (maximum pressure).

touches.haxe_doc: A `TouchList` of all the `Touch` objects representing all current points of contact with the surface, regardless of target or changed status.

targetTouches.haxe_doc: A `TouchList` of all the `Touch` objects that are both currently in contact with the touch surface and were also started on the same element that is the target of the event.

changedTouches.haxe_doc: A `TouchList` of all the `Touch` objects representing individual points of contact whose states changed between the previous touch event and this one.

altKey.haxe_doc: A Boolean value indicating whether or not the alt key was down when the touch event was fired.

metaKey.haxe_doc: A Boolean value indicating whether or not the meta key was down when the touch event was fired.

ctrlKey.haxe_doc: A Boolean value indicating whether or not the control key was down when the touch event was fired.

shiftKey.haxe_doc: A Boolean value indicating whether or not the shift key was down when the touch event was fired.

m.e: { metaKey : false, shiftKey : false, altKey : false, ctrlKey : false, detail : 0, cancelable : false, canBubble : false }

length.haxe_doc: The number of `Touch` objects in the `TouchList`.

item.haxe_doc: Returns the `Touch` object at the specified index in the list.

kind.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` that reflects the `kind` HTML attribute, indicating how the text track is meant to be used. Possible values are: subtitles, captions, descriptions, chapters, metadata.

src.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` that reflects the `src` HTML attribute, indicating the address of the text track data.

srclang.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` that reflects the `srclang` HTML attribute, indicating the language of the text track data.

label.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` that reflects the `label` HTML attribute, indicating a user-readable title for the track.

default_.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` reflects the `default` HTML attribute, indicating that the track is to be enabled if the user's preferences do not indicate that another track would be more appropriate.

readyState.haxe_doc:
Returns  an unsigned short that show the readiness state of the track:
Constant Value Description
NONE 0 Indicates that the text track's cues have not been obtained.
LOADING 1 Indicates that the text track is loading and there have been no fatal errors encountered so far. Further cues might still be added to the track by the parser.
LOADED 2 Indicates that the text track has been loaded with no fatal errors.
ERROR 3 Indicates that the text track was enabled, but when the user agent attempted to obtain it, this failed in some way. Some or all of the cues are likely missing and will not be obtained.

track.haxe_doc: Returns `TextTrack` is the track element's text track data.

root.haxe_doc: Returns a `Node` representing the root node as specified when the `TreeWalker` was created.

whatToShow.haxe_doc:
Returns an unsigned long being a bitmask made of constants describing the types of Node that must be presented. Non-matching nodes are skipped, but their children may be included, if relevant. The possible values are:
Constant Numerical value Description
NodeFilter.SHOW_ALL -1 (that is the max value of unsigned long) Shows all nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_ATTRIBUTE {{deprecated_inline}} 2 Shows attribute Attr nodes. This is meaningful only when creating a TreeWalker with an Attr node as its root. In this case, it means that the attribute node will appear in the first position of the iteration or traversal. Since attributes are never children of other nodes, they do not appear when traversing over the document tree.
NodeFilter.SHOW_CDATA_SECTION {{deprecated_inline}} 8 Shows CDATASection nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_COMMENT 128 Shows Comment nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_DOCUMENT 256 Shows Document nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT 1024 Shows DocumentFragment nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_DOCUMENT_TYPE 512 Shows DocumentType nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_ELEMENT 1 Shows Element nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_ENTITY {{deprecated_inline}} 32 Shows Entity nodes. This is meaningful only when creating a TreeWalker with an Entity node as its root; in this case, it means that the Entity node will appear in the first position of the traversal. Since entities are not part of the document tree, they do not appear when traversing over the document tree.
NodeFilter.SHOW_ENTITY_REFERENCE {{deprecated_inline}} 16 Shows EntityReference nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_NOTATION {{deprecated_inline}} 2048 Shows Notation nodes. This is meaningful only when creating a TreeWalker with a Notation node as its root; in this case, it means that the Notation node will appear in the first position of the traversal. Since entities are not part of the document tree, they do not appear when traversing over the document tree.
NodeFilter.SHOW_PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION 64 Shows ProcessingInstruction nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT 4 Shows Text nodes.

filter.haxe_doc: Returns a `NodeFilter` used to select the relevant nodes.

currentNode.haxe_doc: Is the `Node` on which the `TreeWalker` is currently pointing at.

parentNode.haxe_doc: Moves the current `Node` to the first visible ancestor node in the document order, and returns the found node. It also moves the current node to this one. If no such node exists, or if it is before that the root node defined at the object construction, returns `null` and the current node is not changed. @throws DOMError

firstChild.haxe_doc: Moves the current `Node` to the first visible child of the current node, and returns the found child. It also moves the current node to this child. If no such child exists, returns `null` and the current node is not changed. @throws DOMError

lastChild.haxe_doc: Moves the current `Node` to the last visible child of the current node, and returns the found child. It also moves the current node to this child. If no such child exists, `null` is returned and the current node is not changed. @throws DOMError

previousSibling.haxe_doc: Moves the current `Node` to its previous sibling, if any, and returns the found sibling. If there is no such node, return `null` and the current node is not changed. @throws DOMError

nextSibling.haxe_doc: Moves the current `Node` to its next sibling, if any, and returns the found sibling. If there is no such node, `null` is returned and the current node is not changed. @throws DOMError

previousNode.haxe_doc: Moves the current `Node` to the previous visible node in the document order, and returns the found node. It also moves the current node to this one. If no such node exists, or if it is before that the root node defined at the object construction, returns `null` and the current node is not changed. @throws DOMError

nextNode.haxe_doc: Moves the current `Node` to the next visible node in the document order, and returns the found node. It also moves the current node to this one. If no such node exists, returns `null` and the current node is not changed. @throws DOMError

compact.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` indicating that spacing between list items should be reduced. This property reflects the `compact` attribute only, it doesn't consider the `line-height` CSS property used for that behavior in modern pages.

type.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` value reflecting the `type` and defining the kind of marker to be used to display. The values are browser dependent and have never been standardized.

href.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the whole URL.

origin.haxe_doc: Returns a `DOMString` containing the origin of the URL, that is its scheme, its domain and its port.

protocol.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the protocol scheme of the URL, including the final `':'`.

username.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the username specified before the domain name.

password.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the password specified before the domain name.

host.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the domain (that is the hostname) followed by (if a port was specified) a `':'` and the port of the URL.

hostname.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the domain of the URL.

port.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing the port number of the URL.

pathname.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing an initial `'/'` followed by the path of the URL.

search.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing a `'?'` followed by the parameters of the URL.

searchParams.haxe_doc: Returns a `URLSearchParams` object allowing to access the GET query arguments contained in the URL.

hash.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` containing a `'#'` followed by the fragment identifier of the URL.

append.haxe_doc: Appends a specified key/value pair as a new search parameter.

delete.haxe_doc: Deletes the given search parameter, and its associated value, from the list of all search parameters.

get.haxe_doc: Returns the first value associated to the given search parameter.

getAll.haxe_doc: Returns all the values associated with a given search parameter.

has.haxe_doc: Returns a `Boolean` indicating if such a search parameter exists.

set.haxe_doc: Sets the value associated to a given search parameter to the given value. If there were several values, delete the others.

sort.haxe_doc: Sorts all key/value pairs, if any, by their keys. @throws DOMError

entries.haxe_doc: Returns an `Iteration_protocols` allowing to go through all key/value pairs contained in this object. @throws DOMError

keys.haxe_doc: Returns an `Iteration_protocols` allowing to go through all keys of the key/value pairs contained in this object. @throws DOMError

values.haxe_doc: Returns an `Iteration_protocols` allowing to go through all values of the key/value pairs contained in this object. @throws DOMError

forEach.haxe_doc: @throws DOMError

valueMissing.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` indicating the element has a `required` attribute, but no value.

typeMismatch.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` indicating the value is not in the required syntax (when `type` is `email` or `url`).

patternMismatch.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` indicating the value does not match the specified `pattern`.

tooLong.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` indicating the value exceeds the specified `maxlength` for `HTMLInputElement` or `HTMLTextAreaElement` objects. Note: This will never be `true` in Gecko, because elements' values are prevented from being longer than `maxlength`.

tooShort.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` indicating the value fails to meet the specified `minlength` for `HTMLInputElement` or `HTMLTextAreaElement` objects.

rangeUnderflow.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` indicating the value is less than the minimum specified by the `min` attribute.

rangeOverflow.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` indicating the value is greater than the maximum specified by the `max` attribute.

stepMismatch.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` indicating the value does not fit the rules determined by the `step` attribute (that is, it's not evenly divisible by the step value).

badInput.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` indicating the user has provided input that the browser is unable to convert.

customError.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` indicating the element's custom validity message has been set to a non-empty string by calling the element's `setCustomValidity()` method.

valid.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` indicating the element meets all constraint validations, and is therefore considered to be valid.

width.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` that reflects the `width` HTML attribute, which specifies the width of the display area, in CSS pixels.

height.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` that reflects the `height` HTML attribute, which specifies the height of the display area, in CSS pixels.

videoWidth.haxe_doc: Returns an `unsigned long` containing the intrinsic width of the resource in CSS pixels, taking into account the dimensions, aspect ratio, clean aperture, resolution, and so forth, as defined for the format used by the resource. If the element's ready state is `HAVE_NOTHING`, the value is `0`.

videoHeight.haxe_doc: Returns an `unsigned long` containing the intrinsic height of the resource in CSS pixels, taking into account the dimensions, aspect ratio, clean aperture, resolution, and so forth, as defined for the format used by the resource. If the element's ready state is `HAVE_NOTHING`, the value is `0`.

poster.haxe_doc: Is a `DOMString` that reflects the `poster` HTML attribute, which specifies an image to show while no video data is available.

getVideoPlaybackQuality.haxe_doc: Returns a `VideoPlaybackQuality` objects that contains the current playback metrics.

creationTime.haxe_doc: A `DOMHighResTimeStamp` containing the time in miliseconds since the start of the navigation and the creation of the object.

totalVideoFrames.haxe_doc: An `unsigned long` giving the number of video frames created and dropped since the creation of the associated `HTMLVideoElement`.

droppedVideoFrames.haxe_doc: An `unsigned long` giving the number of video frames dropped since the creation of the associated `HTMLVideoElement`.

corruptedVideoFrames.haxe_doc: An `unsigned long` giving the number of video frames corrupted since the creation of the associated `HTMLVideoElement`. A corrupted frame may be created or dropped.

deltaX.haxe_doc: Returns a `double` representing the horizontal scroll amount.

deltaY.haxe_doc: Returns a `double` representing the vertical scroll amount.

deltaZ.haxe_doc: Returns a `double` representing the scroll amount for the z-axis.

deltaMode.haxe_doc:
Returns an unsigned long representing the unit of the delta values scroll amount. Permitted values are:
Constant Value Description
DOM_DELTA_PIXEL 0x00 The delta values are specified in pixels.
DOM_DELTA_LINE 0x01 The delta values are specified in lines.
DOM_DELTA_PAGE 0x02 The delta values are specified in pages.

window.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the current window.

self.haxe_doc: Returns an object reference to the window object itself.

document.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the document that the window contains.

name.haxe_doc: Gets/sets the name of the window.

location.haxe_doc: Gets/sets the location, or current URL, of the window object.

history.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the history object.

locationbar.haxe_doc: Returns the locationbar object, whose visibility can be toggled in the window.

menubar.haxe_doc: Returns the menubar object, whose visibility can be toggled in the window.

personalbar.haxe_doc: Returns the personalbar object, whose visibility can be toggled in the window.

scrollbars.haxe_doc: Returns the scrollbars object, whose visibility can be toggled in the window.

statusbar.haxe_doc: Returns the statusbar object, whose visibility can be toggled in the window.

toolbar.haxe_doc: Returns the toolbar object, whose visibility can be toggled in the window.

status.haxe_doc: Gets/sets the text in the statusbar at the bottom of the browser.

closed.haxe_doc: This property indicates whether the current window is closed or not.

event.haxe_doc: Returns the current event, which is the event currently being handled by the JavaScript code's context, or `undefined` if no event is currently being handled. The `Event` object passed directly to event handlers should be used instead whenever possible.

frames.haxe_doc: Returns an array of the subframes in the current window.

length.haxe_doc: Returns the number of frames in the window. See also `window.frames`.

top.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the topmost window in the window hierarchy. This property is read only.

opener.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the window that opened this current window.

parent.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the parent of the current window or subframe.

frameElement.haxe_doc: Returns the element in which the window is embedded, or null if the window is not embedded.

navigator.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the navigator object.

console.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the console object which provides access to the browser's debugging console.

screen.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the screen object associated with the window.

innerWidth.haxe_doc: Gets the width of the content area of the browser window including, if rendered, the vertical scrollbar.

innerHeight.haxe_doc: Gets the height of the content area of the browser window including, if rendered, the horizontal scrollbar.

scrollX.haxe_doc: Returns the number of pixels that the document has already been scrolled horizontally.

scrollY.haxe_doc: Returns the number of pixels that the document has already been scrolled vertically.

screenX.haxe_doc: Returns the horizontal distance of the left border of the user's browser from the left side of the screen.

screenY.haxe_doc: Returns the vertical distance of the top border of the user's browser from the top side of the screen.

outerWidth.haxe_doc: Gets the width of the outside of the browser window.

outerHeight.haxe_doc: Gets the height of the outside of the browser window.

performance.haxe_doc: Returns a `Performance` object, which includes the `Performance.timing` and `Performance.navigation` attributes, each of which is an object providing performance-related data. See also Using Navigation Timing for additional information and examples.

devicePixelRatio.haxe_doc: Returns the ratio between physical pixels and device independent pixels in the current display.

scrollMaxX.haxe_doc: The maximum offset that the window can be scrolled to horizontally, that is the document width minus the viewport width.

scrollMaxY.haxe_doc: The maximum offset that the window can be scrolled to vertically (i.e., the document height minus the viewport height).

fullScreen.haxe_doc: This property indicates whether the window is displayed in full screen or not.

content.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the content element in the current window. Since Firefox 57 (initially Nightly-only), both versions are only available from chrome (privileged) code, and not available to the web anymore.

orientation.haxe_doc: Returns the orientation in degrees (in 90 degree increments) of the viewport relative to the device's natural orientation.

speechSynthesis.haxe_doc: Returns a `SpeechSynthesis` object, which is the entry point into using Web Speech API speech synthesis functionality.

localStorage.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the local storage object used to store data that may only be accessed by the origin that created it.

isSecureContext.haxe_doc: Indicates whether a context is capable of using features that require secure contexts.

sessionStorage.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the session storage object used to store data that may only be accessed by the origin that created it.

stop.haxe_doc: This method stops window loading. @throws DOMError

focus.haxe_doc: Sets focus on the current window. @throws DOMError

blur.haxe_doc: Sets focus away from the window. @throws DOMError

confirm.haxe_doc: Displays a dialog with a message that the user needs to respond to. @throws DOMError

prompt.haxe_doc: Returns the text entered by the user in a prompt dialog. @throws DOMError

print.haxe_doc: Opens the Print Dialog to print the current document. @throws DOMError

postMessage.haxe_doc: Provides a secure means for one window to send a string of data to another window, which need not be within the same domain as the first. @throws DOMError

captureEvents.haxe_doc: Registers the window to capture all events of the specified type.

releaseEvents.haxe_doc: Releases the window from trapping events of a specific type.

getSelection.haxe_doc: Returns the selection object representing the selected item(s). @throws DOMError

getComputedStyle.haxe_doc: Gets computed style for the specified element. Computed style indicates the computed values of all CSS properties of the element. @throws DOMError

matchMedia.haxe_doc: Returns a `MediaQueryList` object representing the specified media query string. @throws DOMError

moveTo.haxe_doc: Moves the window to the specified coordinates. @throws DOMError

moveBy.haxe_doc: Moves the current window by a specified amount. @throws DOMError

resizeBy.haxe_doc: Resizes the current window by a certain amount. @throws DOMError

scroll.haxe_doc: Scrolls the window to a particular place in the document.
Scrolls the window to a particular place in the document.

scrollTo.haxe_doc: Scrolls to a particular set of coordinates in the document.
Scrolls to a particular set of coordinates in the document.

scrollBy.haxe_doc: Scrolls the document in the window by the given amount.
Scrolls the document in the window by the given amount.

requestAnimationFrame.haxe_doc: Tells the browser that an animation is in progress, requesting that the browser schedule a repaint of the window for the next animation frame. @throws DOMError

cancelAnimationFrame.haxe_doc: Enables you to cancel a callback previously scheduled with `Window.requestAnimationFrame`. @throws DOMError

getDefaultComputedStyle.haxe_doc: Gets default computed style for the specified element, ignoring author stylesheets. @throws DOMError

scrollByLines.haxe_doc: Scrolls the document by the given number of lines.

scrollByPages.haxe_doc: Scrolls the current document by the specified number of pages.

sizeToContent.haxe_doc: Sizes the window according to its content. @throws DOMError

updateCommands.haxe_doc: Updates the state of commands of the current chrome window (UI).

m.e: { showDialog : false, searchInFrames : false, wholeWord : false, wrapAround : false, backwards : false, caseSensitive : false, str : "" }

find.haxe_doc: Searches for a given string in a window. @throws DOMError

dump.haxe_doc: Writes a message to the console.

structuredClone.haxe_doc: Creates a deep clone of a given value using the structured clone algorithm.

setResizable.haxe_doc: Toggles a user's ability to resize a window.

self.haxe_doc: Returns a reference to the `WorkerGlobalScope` itself. Most of the time it is a specific scope like `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`, `SharedWorkerGlobalScope` or `ServiceWorkerGlobalScope`.

location.haxe_doc: Returns the `WorkerLocation` associated with the worker. It is a specific location object, mostly a subset of the `Location` for browsing scopes, but adapted to workers.

onerror.haxe_doc: Is an `EventHandler` representing the code to be called when the `error` event is raised.

onoffline.haxe_doc: Is an `EventHandler` representing the code to be called when the `offline` event is raised.

ononline.haxe_doc: Is an `EventHandler` representing the code to be called when the `online` event is raised.

performance.haxe_doc: Returns the `Performance` associated with the worker. It is a regular performance object, except that only a subset of its property and methods are available to workers.

importScripts.haxe_doc: Imports one or more scripts into the worker's scope. You can specify as many as you'd like, separated by commas. For example:` importScripts('foo.js', 'bar.js');` @throws DOMError

dump.haxe_doc: Allows you to write a message to stdout — i.e. in your terminal. This is the same as Firefox's `window.dump`, but for workers.

structuredClone.haxe_doc: Creates a deep clone of a given value using the structured clone algorithm.

onreadystatechange.haxe_doc: An `EventHandler` that is called whenever the `readyState` attribute changes.

readyState.haxe_doc: Returns an `unsigned short`, the state of the request.

timeout.haxe_doc: Is an `unsigned long` representing the number of milliseconds a request can take before automatically being terminated.

withCredentials.haxe_doc: Is a `Boolean` that indicates whether or not cross-site `Access-Control` requests should be made using credentials such as cookies or authorization headers.

upload.haxe_doc: Is an `XMLHttpRequestUpload`, representing the upload process.

responseURL.haxe_doc: Returns the serialized URL of the response or the empty string if the URL is null.

status.haxe_doc: Returns an `unsigned short` with the status of the response of the request.

statusText.haxe_doc: Returns a `DOMString` containing the response string returned by the HTTP server. Unlike `XMLHTTPRequest.status`, this includes the entire text of the response message ("`200 OK`", for example).

responseType.haxe_doc: Is an enumerated value that defines the response type.

response.haxe_doc: Returns an `ArrayBuffer`, `Blob`, `Document`, JavaScript object, or a `DOMString`, depending on the value of `XMLHttpRequest.responseType`. that contains the response entity body.

responseText.haxe_doc: Returns a `DOMString` that contains the response to the request as text, or `null` if the request was unsuccessful or has not yet been sent.

responseXML.haxe_doc: Returns a `Document` containing the response to the request, or `null` if the request was unsuccessful, has not yet been sent, or cannot be parsed as XML or HTML.

numberOfOutputs.haxe_doc: Returns the number of outputs coming out of the node. Destination nodes — like `AudioDestinationNode` — have a value of `0` for this attribute.

channelCountMode.haxe_doc: Represents an enumerated value describing the way channels must be matched between the node's inputs and outputs.
